svg.title: A schema.toml attribute block on the left; four example declarations routed by their flags to three storage homes — the hot column read per rendered mark, the entity-space search structure read per query, and the record blob read per click.
svg.text: One TOML block per field decides where its bytes live — and therefore when they are ever read

g.text: [[attribute]]
name = "archive"
type = "category" # or a number width,
width = "u8" # timestamp, keyword, text
render = true # drawn on the map
index = true # searchable / filterable
vocabulary = "declared" # or discovered at ingest
listing = "public" # who may learn the value list

svg.text: WHAT THE BUILD DOES WITH IT

g.text: tessera build compiles the schema into the bundle's
MANIFEST; the engine serves only what it declares, and
/v1/meta advertises the filter operands derived from it
name and type are required; every flag defaults to false —
the cheapest placement, made costlier only by an explicit word
categories must also declare width, vocabulary and listing:
disclosure and migration controls never default

svg.text: WHERE THE BYTES LIVE — ONE HOME PER FIELD, CHOSEN BY THE FLAGS

g.text: recency — f32
archive — category (u8)
submitter — keyword
doi — keyword
render = true
render + index
index = true
no flags
row space, fixed width, mmap'd — read per rendered
mark (~10⁵ a viewport); never compressed
entity space, scanned under the viewer's mask — read
once per query; categories add per-value bitmaps
compressed blocks (3.0× measured) — one block read
per click (~0.25 ms); never on the render or query path
the routing rule: place by how often a value is read, not by what it is — per mark, per query and per click are four orders of magnitude apart
store once: a field's bytes live in exactly one home; a rendered column is already filterable over the request's own rows, at no extra storage
refused at parse, each naming itself: render on keyword or text (not fixed width), render on a multi-valued field, a category missing its controls
